title: Specialized Plant Structures
seo_title: Grade 5 Science: Specialized Plant Structures Worksheets (MATATAG)
standard_text: Plants have specialized structures (roots, stems, leaves, flowers, fruits and seeds) that help them get water and food, reproduce and survive in their environment. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 5, Quarter 2: Living Things)
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 2: Living Things): parts of a plant, how water moves, flowers and pollination, seed dispersal and plant adaptations. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Each plant part has a job.
key_sub: Some plant parts are specialized to help the plant survive.
body_html:
How to think about it

Roots anchor the plant and take in water and minerals; stems support the plant and carry water and food; leaves make food by photosynthesis. Flowers make seeds; fruits protect and spread seeds.

Some plants have specialized structures: cactus stems store water and their leaves are spines; mangrove roots stick up out of the mud to get air; the leaves of a water lily float. Seeds are spread by wind, water, animals and bursting pods.

Example

Why do mangroves have roots that stick up?

Muddy, wet soil

Answer: to get air

Example

How is a coconut spread?

It floats.

Answer: by water

Common mistakes

  • Thinking roots only hold the plant.
  • Thinking all seeds are spread by animals.
  • Thinking leaves take in water from the soil.

faq.q: Why do some seeds have wings?
faq.a: So that the wind can carry them far from the parent plant.

faq.q: Why are some flowers brightly colored?
faq.a: To attract insects and birds that carry pollen.

items.q: Which plant part do we eat when we eat carrots?

items.q: What does the stem do?

items.q: Why does a bunch of flowers slowly use up the water in its vase?
c: The water turns into air on its own only at night.
The stems take up water, and it evaporates from the leaves and petals.
items.e: Water moves up and out.

items.q: Cut flowers in a vase stay fresh longer if you trim their stems. Why?
c: It stops the flowers growing roots.
A fresh cut lets water travel up the stem more easily.
items.e: Fresh tubes take up water.

items.q: Water moves through a plant. Which does the water pass through first: the leaves and flowers or the stem?
c: Water does not pass through either.
They happen at the same time.
items.e: Soil → roots → stem → leaves and flowers → out into the air.

items.q: Water moves through a plant. Where was the water just before it reached the leaves and flowers?
items.e: Soil → roots → stem → leaves and flowers → out into the air.

items.q: Water moves through a plant. Which does the water pass through first: the leaves and flowers or the roots?

They happen at the same time.

items.q: Why does a plant in a sunny window need watering more often than one in a shady corner?
c: More water evaporates from its leaves.
items.e: Warm and sunny: more evaporation.

items.q: Kevin stood a white lily in a jar of water with blue food coloring. When the stem is cut across, what will Kevin see?
c: small blue dots, which are the ends of the water tubes

items.e: The tubes carry the water up the stem.

items.q: A tree is very tall. How does water reach the top leaves?
c: It does not reach the top.
It travels up tiny tubes in the trunk.
Rain falls straight into the top leaves only.
items.e: A trunk is a stem.

items.q: Mark stood a white tulip in a jar of water with blue food coloring. Where will the blue color appear after a day?
c: nowhere, the color stays in the jar
only at the bottom of the stem
items.e: The colored water travels up the stem to the top of the plant.

items.q: A plant is pulled up and its roots are washed clean of soil. Why might it wilt after replanting?
c: Many tiny root hairs were damaged, so it takes in less water.
Roots do not take in water.
Soil is not needed for water.
items.e: Root hairs take in water.

items.q: A pot plant's leaves droop on a hot day. What will help it most?
items.e: Roots take up the water.

items.q: Why do leaves feel cooler than the air on a hot day?
c: Water evaporating from them cools them down.
items.e: Like sweat.

items.q: Kenneth stood a white lily in a jar of water with purple food coloring. Why does the color spread up the plant?
c: The color floats up through the air.
The plant takes up the colored water through tiny tubes in its stem.
items.e: The tubes carry water up from the bottom.

items.q: Why does a plant droop (wilt) when it does not get enough water?
c: There is not enough water in the stem and leaves to keep them firm.
items.e: Water keeps plants firm.

items.q: Is the stigma part of the male or the female part of a flower?
items.e: The stamen (anther and filament) is male; the pistil (stigma, style and ovary) is female.

items.q: What does the ovule of a flower do?
c: It contains the female reproductive cell and becomes the seed.
It receives pollen; it is often sticky.
items.e: The ovule contains the female reproductive cell and becomes the seed.

items.q: Rose sees a hummingbird near some plants. How can it help the plants?
c: It moves pollen while drinking nectar.
It carries sticky seeds in its fur.
It eats berries and drops the seeds far away.
items.e: A hummingbird helps with pollination.

items.q: Lance sees a squirrel near some plants. How can it help the plants?
c: It buries acorns that grow into new trees.
It moves pollen while drinking nectar.
It moves pollen from flower to flower.
items.e: A squirrel helps with seed dispersal.

items.q: What does the anther of a flower do?
c: It contains the ovules and becomes the fruit.
It receives pollen; it is often sticky.
It connects the stigma to the ovary.
items.e: The anther makes pollen.

items.q: A flower has sticky or spiky pollen grains. How is it most likely pollinated?
items.e: Insect-pollinated flowers attract insects; wind-pollinated flowers make light pollen that is blown about.

items.q: Diane watches a bee. A bee moves pollen from flower to flower. How is it helping plants?

items.q: How are the seeds of a sycamore usually dispersed?

items.q: Which is a way people use plants?

items.e: This structure is suited to spreading seeds to new islands.

items.q: Which plant can be used to make medicine?

items.q: How do beans help corn and squash in a Three Sisters garden?

items.q: Which structure helps a sunflower with growing tall above other plants to get sunlight?
